name: nexiguran ziclumeran
summary: Nexiguran ziclumeran (nex-z, NTLA-2001) is Intellia's in vivo CRISPR/Cas9 edit of TTR in the liver, a single 55 mg IV infusion, co-developed with Regeneron (Intellia leads; Regeneron shares about 25% of worldwide development costs and commercial profits). DUPLICATE IN THE BOOK: asset 2584 'NTLA-2001' (NTLA) is the same molecule. The book's trials table maps MAGNITUDE (NCT06128629) to 2584 and MAGNITUDE-2 (NCT06672237) to 2581, so seed this asset once, on 2581 (nexiguran ziclumeran), and do not seed 2584, or the molecule is counted twice. Status, from Intellia's 2026 filings: the FDA hold of 2025-10-29 (Grade 4 liver injury; the patient died 2025-11-05) was lifted for MAGNITUDE-2 (ATTRv-PN, 50 patients, mNIS+7 at month 18) in January 2026 and for MAGNITUDE (ATTR-CM, about 1,200 patients, CV death and events) in March 2026. Screening resumed in Q2 2026, and MAGNITUDE-2 enrolment is due to complete in H2 2026. In August 2026 the highest liver elevations were traced to one HLA allele (C*05:01, about 12% carriers). Price anchor: Casgevy's $2.2mm with Zolgensma's 36% off list, net $1.408mm, as the verified lonvo-z seed takes it. Uptake anchor: half of Amvuttra's measured US start rates, recomputed at a patient-year price from the book's Part B demand rows: $451,674 net, four 25 mg doses at $4,787.75 a mg less the 6% add-on. That gives 5.87% a year of the ATTR-CM pool in its CM launch and 11.40% of the ATTRv-PN pool in 2024, so peaks of 0.0293 and 0.0570. The researcher's 0.037 and 0.0719 divided revenue by spend per beneficiary, which covers only 3.17 of the 4 annual doses. PN's first full year is 2030 and CM's a year later. Engine: peak product revenue about $4.2bn (2038, US $3.2bn), before Intellia's 0.695 share and probability of success. Pools: the book carries no ATTR pool. The CM figures (55,372 and 25,605, Alexander JAHA 2026) and PN figures (5,161 and 1,196, Laires Open Heart 2025) were checked against the papers. The CM figures equal the unverified nucresiran seed's and must stay identical to it. The book also maps 'Amyloidosis' to AL assets (etentamig, daratumumab, Blenrep), and those must not read this ATTR-CM pool.

therapy_mode.source: Intellia 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-337952, filed 2026-08-06), MD&A: MAGNITUDE 'Patients are randomized 2:1 nex-z:placebo, with a single 55 mg infusion of nex-z administered'; MAGNITUDE-2 'Patients will be randomized 1:1 to receive a single 55 mg infusion of nex-z or placebo'; nex-z offers 'a deep, consistent and potentially lifelong reduction in TTR protein after a one-time treatment'
therapy_mode.note: One infusion, not repeated, billed once, so each year's treated patients are that year's revenue. Same mode as the sister asset lonvo-z (verified NTLA_biological_ntla_2002.json) and the book's Casgevy seed. Re-dosing is not modelled
therapy_mode.check: Q2 2026 10-Q (0001193125-26-337952) MD&A in the book's filing_sections, verbatim: MAGNITUDE 'Patients are randomized 2:1 nex-z:placebo, with a single 55 mg infusion of nex-z administered'; MAGNITUDE-2 'Patients will be randomized 1:1 to receive a single 55 mg infusion of nex-z or placebo'; nex-z drives 'a deep, consistent and potentially lifelong reduction in TTR protein after a one-time treatment'. One infusion billed once is one_time, as the verified lonvo-z seed and the book's Casgevy seed (lookup.py seed Exagamglogene: therapy_mode one_time).

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py seed Exagamglogene autotemcel: list_price_per_patient 2.2 mm USD, 'Vertex, Dec 2023 launch price' (Casgevy, the only marketed CRISPR/Cas9 therapy), the anchor the verified lonvo-z seed uses. Cross-check against the chronic incumbents, lookup.py demand, CMS 2024 per beneficiary: Amvuttra Part B $379,824 ($229,033,878.80 / 603); Amvuttra Part D $118,225 a fill ($140,924,646.88 / 1,192 claims), $472,900 at four quarterly fills; Vyndamax Part D $203,290; Wainua Part D $226,539. Time on chronic therapy: in Optum, 13 of 111 vutrisiran starters died and 10 stopped for good within 12 months, 20.72% a year (Bart NK et al., Adv Ther 2026, doi:10.1007/s12325-026-03664-7, PMID 42455256), a mean of 4.83 years
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the anchor, kept consistent with lonvo-z (same company, same LNP-delivered Cas9 modality). Intellia has set no price and suspended nex-z milestone guidance during the hold (8-K 0001193125-25-269479); no management pricing comment was found (searched). $2.2mm is 5.8 years of Amvuttra's Part B spend per beneficiary, 4.7 years at four Part D fills, and 10.8 years of Vyndamax. At the Amvuttra net the book uses ($358,324, Part B less the 6% add-on) and a 4.83-year mean time on therapy, a patient's expected lifetime net cost on Amvuttra is $1.73mm; nex-z's $1.408mm net (below) is 81% of that, so the one-time price sits at rough parity with chronic silencing. Case for lower: ATTR-CM patients are old (mean age 77.9 among narrow-definition incident ATTR-CM cases in Laires 2025, PMID 41469145) and mostly Medicare, a $2.2mm upfront Part B claim carries a large budget impact, the liver-safety signal may weaken the value case, and generic tafamidis meglumine may arrive after compound patent 7214695 expires on 2026-12-19 (book exclusivities table; a further Vyndamax substance patent, 9770441, runs to 2035-08-31). Case for higher: hATTR-PN patients are younger (mean age 67.4 in Laires's PN-only cohort) with more years of chronic therapy to replace
list_price_per_patient.check: Anchor: lookup.py seed Exagamglogene autotemcel carries list_price_per_patient 2.2 mm USD ('Vertex, Dec 2023 launch price (workbook C9)'). The verified lonvo-z seed takes the same anchor, and its reader confirmed Casgevy's $2.2mm WAC by web search, so the two Intellia edits share one convention as instructed. Cross-checks recomputed from lookup.py demand (CMS 2024): Amvuttra Part B $229,033,878.80 / 603 = $379,824; Part D $140,924,646.88 / 1,192 claims = $118,225 a fill, x4 = $472,901; Vyndamax Part D $203,290; Wainua Part D $226,539. So 2.2 / 0.379824 = 5.79, 2.2 / 0.4729 = 4.65 and 2.2 / 0.20329 = 10.82 years, as stated. Bart 2026 (PMID 42455256 abstract, doi:10.1007/s12325-026-03664-7): 'Within 12 months of vutrisiran initiation, 13 (12%) patients died and an additional 13 (12%) discontinued therapy, of which 3 (23%) restarted vutrisiran and 10 (77%) switched ATTR therapy'. So 23 / 111 = 20.72% left vutrisiran, and 1 / 0.2072 = 4.83 years. The note's 'stopped for good' should read 'switched to another ATTR therapy'. Lifetime cost at $358,324 is $1.73mm, and 1.408 / 1.73 = 81%, as stated. However, the same Part B row shows that a 2024 beneficiary received 47,837.5 mg / 25 / 603 = 3.17 of 4 annual doses. A patient-year therefore costs $478,775 allowed, or $451,674 at ASP. On that basis the lifetime net is $2.18mm and nex-z's $1.408mm is 65% of it, which strengthens the case for higher. Laires full text (PMC12766817, Table 1) confirms the mean ages: 77.9 (narrow incident ATTR-CM) and 67.4 (narrow ATTR-PN only). Tafamidis patents: the book's exclusivities for Vyndamax (asset 43) list 7214695 (substance) to 2026-12-19 and 9770441 (substance) to 2035-08-31. The suspended milestone guidance is confirmed verbatim in 8-K 0001193125-25-269479 EX-99.1. A labelled judgement whose inputs hold.

gross_to_net_pct.source: Zolgensma (onasemnogene abeparvovec, one-time IV gene therapy): CMS reimbursement had fallen to $1.36mm per claim by 2022 against a $2.125mm list, 'nearly a 40% discount' (BioSpace, 'Who's Paying for Million-Dollar Gene Therapies?', biospace.com/who-s-paying-for-million-dollar-gene-therapies; read from the search summary by the lonvo-z researcher and second reader). 1 - 1.36/2.125 = 0.36. Same value and source as the verified lonvo-z seed
gross_to_net_pct.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator, kept consistent with lonvo-z. The anchor is a list price, so neither house Medicare convention applies. Direction checked: 0.36 is the share off list, net $1.408mm per course. Case for lower (less off list): ATTR patients are mostly Medicare, and an infused product billed under Part B is paid at ASP plus 6%; ASP excludes Medicaid rebates, so a Medicare-heavy product may be discounted less than Zolgensma, whose SMA infants carry a large Medicaid share. The book's Casgevy seed assumes about 18%. Case for higher: payers facing a Medicare-scale budget may demand outcomes-based or annuity contracts
gross_to_net_pct.check: This is the same value and source as the verified lonvo-z seed, whose second reader confirmed BioSpace's 'By 2022, the reimbursement for Zolgensma dropped to $1.36 million per claim, nearly a 40% discount from its list price' against a $2.125mm list. It is kept for consistency across Intellia's two one-time edits, as instructed, and was not re-searched. 1 - 1.36 / 2.125 = 0.36. The direction is right (share off list), so net = 2.2 x 0.64 = $1.408mm. The Casgevy seed's roughly 18% is confirmed (lookup.py seed: net_price_per_patient 1.8 on a 2.2 list, 'workbook C10'). The Medicare-heavy case for lower is stated.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: one infusion, not repeated (Intellia 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-337952, filed 2026-08-06), MD&A)
discontinuation_pct.note: Set so the engine never carries a treated stock forward in either mode; one_time mode ignores it. Same as lonvo-z
discontinuation_pct.check: Inert in one_time mode: forecast.py reads it only in the chronic branch, as the lonvo-z reader found. The single infusion is confirmed in the Q2 2026 10-Q. Same value as lonvo-z.

cogs_per_patient.source: none found: Intellia has no product revenue and discloses no cost of goods for nex-z (10-K FY2025 0001193125-26-076550; 10-Qs 0001193125-26-215740 and 0001193125-26-337952 in the book's filing_sections)
cogs_per_patient.note: Left null, as for lonvo-z. With it null in one_time mode the engine charges cogs_pct x revenue, and the NTLA company rows now in data/assumptions/ntla_biological_ntla_2002.csv carry cogs_pct 0.1823 borrowed from ALNY. The book's Casgevy 0.75 is an ex vivo estimate and does not transfer to an LNP-delivered mRNA and guide RNA
cogs_per_patient.check: Null accepted. Intellia has no product revenue. The lonvo-z reader's regex over the FY2025 10-K and the Q2 2026 10-Q found no cost-of-goods wording. data/assumptions/ntla_biological_ntla_2002.csv carries NTLA cogs_pct 0.1823 (ALNY's row, labelled a comparator), so the engine charges 18.23% of revenue. The Casgevy 0.75 is 'est. 500k-1mm manufacturing cost' for ex vivo manufacture (lookup.py seed) and is rightly not carried.

forecast_start_year.source: MAGNITUDE-2: 47 patients enrolled when the hold began (Q3 2025 release, 8-K 0001193125-25-269479, which also 'suspended its milestone guidance for nex-z'); hold lifted January 2026 (8-K 0001193125-26-023387); 'We remain on track to complete patient enrollment in MAGNITUDE-2 in the second half of 2026', with primary endpoints 'mNIS+7 at month 18 and serum TTR at day 29' (Intellia 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-337952, filed 2026-08-06), MD&A). MAGNITUDE: more than 650 of about 1,200 enrolled at the hold (8-K 0001193125-25-269479); hold lifted March 2026 (8-K 0001193125-26-084309); registry primary completion 2027-12, estimated (book trials table, last update 2026-03-27)
forecast_start_year.note: JUDGEMENT. First full year for ATTRv-PN: enrolment completes in H2 2026, so the last patient reaches month 18 in 2028 at the earliest, topline follows in 2028, a BLA around the turn of 2029, and approval in 2029 on a standard or priority review. 2030 is the first full year. The pre-hold goal of a BLA 'by 2028' (Intellia's MAGNITUDE-2 releases of 2025, read from search summaries) was suspended in November 2025 and not restated in 2026. DISCREPANCY: the registry's MAGNITUDE-2 primary completion of 2027-07 (context file; last update 2026-04-16) cannot hold against an 18-month endpoint on enrolment that completes in H2 2026. ATTR-CM is placed a year later (ramp_midpoint_year of its block is offset by 1.0): the registry's 2027-12 is stale for the same reason, the trial lost about six months to the hold with fewer than 550 patients still to enrol, and the CV-outcomes readout is event-driven, so a readout around 2029 and a supplemental approval in 2030 make 2031 its first full year. Case for later: HLA engagement with the FDA could force a further amendment, and comparable ATTR-CM outcome trials ran 30 to 36 months. Case for earlier: the book's two-calendar-years-after-completion rule on the registry dates would give 2029 for both
forecast_start_year.check: Status, from the book's filing_sections. Q2 2026 10-Q MD&A: 'In January 2026, we announced that the FDA lifted the clinical hold on the IND for MAGNITUDE-2 ... In March 2026, we announced that the FDA lifted the clinical hold on the IND for MAGNITUDE'. Risk factors: 'In the first quarter of 2026, the FDA removed the clinical holds'. The 8-Ks of 2026-01-27 (0001193125-26-023387) and 2026-03-02 (0001193125-26-084309) are in the filings table. Q1 2026 release (0001193125-26-215721): 'Recently resumed patient screening'. Q2 2026 release (0001193125-26-336772): 'Enrollment successfully reinitiated ... MAGNITUDE-2 enrollment in ATTRv-PN expected to be completed in second half of 2026'. The 10-Q gives primary endpoints of 'mNIS+7 at month 18 and serum TTR at day 29' and MAGNITUDE-2 at '50 adults' (the registry says 60). Q3 2025 release (0001193125-25-269479): 'More than 650 patients with ATTR-CM are currently enrolled in MAGNITUDE, and 47 patients with ATTRv-PN are enrolled in MAGNITUDE-2', and 'the company has suspended its milestone guidance for nex-z'. HLA: the Q2 2026 10-Q and release confirm the August 2026 finding. Book trials table: NCT06128629 primary completion 2027-12, estimated (last update 2026-03-27); NCT06672237 primary completion 2027-07, estimated (last update 2026-04-16). Timing check: enrolment ends H2 2026, the last patient reaches month 18 in H1 to H2 2028, and topline follows in 2028. A web search surfaces Intellia pages stating a BLA for ATTRv-PN 'by 2028', but none of the 2026 filings in the book restates it. Approval would then come in late 2029 (priority) or 2030 (standard), so 2030 as the first full year is a fair judgement and 2031 is a real risk for PN. The CM offset of a year is a labelled judgement. The registry dates are stale, as noted. Amass TrialCore was unavailable (usage limit), so the book's trials rows are the check.

exus_multiple.source: Amvuttra, Alnylam FY2025 10-K (0001628280-26-007497), book asset_revenue_regions: US $1,731.222mm, Europe $405.899mm, rest of world $176.715mm. (405.899 + 176.715) / 1,731.222 = 0.3365. The same figure the ALNY nucresiran seed takes
exus_multiple.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator: the TTR silencer in the same two diseases, launched worldwide by a US biotech that built its own ex-US business. Regeneron's co/co is worldwide, with Intellia as lead party. Case for lower: Intellia has no ex-US commercial presence, the lonvo-z seed takes Orladeyo's 0.1173 for that reason, and European HTA bodies have been slow to pay $2mm-plus one-time prices. Case for higher: ex-US hATTR-PN is a larger share of the disease (Amvuttra's PN-only FY2024 split read 0.539, (235.441 + 104.396) / 630.613), and tafamidis reads 0.664 (Pfizer FY2025)
exus_multiple.check: Book asset_revenue_regions, Amvuttra (asset 122) FY2025: US $1,731.222mm, Europe $405.899mm, NonUSOrEurope $176.715mm. (405.899 + 176.715) / 1,731.222 = 0.33653. PN-era FY2024: (235.441 + 104.396) / 630.613 = 0.5389. Tafamidis (asset 1310) FY2025: Int'l $2,546mm / US $3,834mm = 0.664. The Q2 2026 10-Q says Regeneron shares in 'worldwide' costs and profits. A labelled judgement whose inputs hold. One simplification: a single multiple scales both blocks, although ex-US is a larger share of PN.

economics_share.source: Intellia 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-337952, filed 2026-08-06), MD&A: 'Nex-z is the subject of a co-development and co-promotion ("Co/Co") agreement (the "ATTR Co/Co") with Regeneron, for which we are the clinical and commercial lead party and Regeneron is the participating party. Regeneron shares in approximately 25% of worldwide development costs and commercial profits for the ATTR program and has an option to enter into a co-promotion agreement for the U.S. commercialization.' Same wording in the Q1 2026 10-Q (0001193125-26-215740). Royalty: Intellia 10-K FY2024 (0000950170-25-029007), Regeneron collaboration note: 'the Company's existing low- to mid-single-digit royalty obligations under a license agreement with Caribou'; the 2026 10-Qs say Intellia may pay royalties on product sales using technology 'sublicensed from third parties, including Caribou'. Margin from the NTLA company rows in data/assumptions/ntla_biological_ntla_2002.csv: 1 - 0.1823 (cogs) - 0.326 (sga) - 0.3554 (rd) - 0 (other) = 0.1363
economics_share.note: 0.75 x (0.1363 - 0.01) / 0.1363 = 0.75 x 0.926632 = 0.694974. Intellia keeps 75% of the co/co's profits; the Caribou royalty is read at the bottom of 'low- to mid-single-digit', 1% of net sales (the lonvo-z seed's reading), and netted by the house rule for a royalty paid, (margin - royalty) / margin. JUDGEMENT that the royalty is a shared programme cost, so Intellia bears 75% of it; the filings do not say. If Intellia bears it alone, the share is 0.75 - 0.01 / 0.1363 = 0.676632. At the top of the range (say 5%), 0.75 x (0.1363 - 0.05) / 0.1363 = 0.4750, so the royalty rate matters on a margin this thin. Regeneron's co-promotion option does not change the split
economics_share.check: Regeneron wording verbatim in the Q1 2026 (0001193125-26-215740) and Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-337952) 10-Q MD&A: 'we are the clinical and commercial lead party and Regeneron is the participating party. Regeneron shares in approximately 25% of worldwide development costs and commercial profits for the ATTR program and has an option to enter into a co-promotion agreement for the U.S. commercialization.' Caribou: the FY2024 10-K (0000950170-25-029007) collaboration note says the royalties Regeneron pays on its non-Co/Co products 'incorporate the Company's existing low- to mid-single-digit royalty obligations under a license agreement with Caribou'. The 2026 10-Qs say Intellia may pay royalties 'based on our revenues, including sales revenues of our products, utilizing the technologies ... sublicensed from third parties, including Caribou'. Shared or Intellia's alone: no filing in the book says whether the Caribou royalty is charged to the ATTR Co/Co P&L, and a web search (sec.gov results) found no Co/Co cost-sharing terms. The one filed analogue, where the rate Regeneron pays already incorporates Intellia's Caribou obligation, shows the partners built the Caribou burden into their split rather than leaving it with Intellia. That supports the shared reading, so the judgement stands. Recomputed: margin 1 - 0.1823 - 0.326 - 0.3554 - 0 = 0.1363 (NTLA rows in data/assumptions/ntla_biological_ntla_2002.csv confirmed). 0.75 x (0.1363 - 0.01) / 0.1363 = 0.75 x 0.926632 = 0.694974. Borne by Intellia alone, it would be 0.75 - 0.01 / 0.1363 = 0.676632 (2.6% lower). At a 5% shared royalty it is 0.4749. The 1% tier matches the lonvo-z CSV's 0.926632.

prevalence.source: Alexander KM et al., 'Temporal Trends in Incidence and Prevalence of Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy in the United States', J Am Heart Assoc 2026;15(13):e047135, doi:10.1161/JAHA.125.047135, PMID 42333670 (abstract confirmed on PubMed): ATTR-CM prevalence 95.8 per 100,000 (95% CI 89.2-102.4) aged 65 and over in 2022 (Merative MarketScan Medicare). x 57.8mm US residents aged 65 and over in 2022 (US Census Bureau, census.gov/newsroom/stories/older-americans-month.html) = 55,372
prevalence.note: This block is ATTR-CM (MAGNITUDE, NCT06128629). lookup.py pool (Amyloid, Transthyretin, ATTR, Cardiomyopath) and epidemiology.csv return nothing, so the book does not yet carry it. The figure is IDENTICAL to the one the ALNY nucresiran seed (out/ALNY_nucresiran.json) carries for the same indication name, so one disease keeps one number; if that seed's second read changes it, this must follow. 'Amyloidosis' is the broad MeSH name the book also maps to AL assets (etentamig, daratumumab, belantamab); they must not read this pool. Diagnosed, wild-type and hereditary, 65 and over. It includes mixed CM-and-PN patients, about 3,349 on Laires's narrow rate (9.8 per million x 341.78mm), who also sit in the PN block below
prevalence.check: Alexander 2026 full text (PMC13477393, doi:10.1161/JAHA.125.047135): prevalence per 100,000 was '95.8 (95% CI, 89.3-102.6) in 2022 in the Medicare Database' (the abstract prints 89.2-102.4). It is counted on the 1 January index date among MarketScan Medicare Supplement and, from 2020, Medicare Advantage enrollees aged 65 and over. The abstract's '2010-2021' is the incidence window; prevalence runs to 2022. Census 'Older Americans Month: May 2023' (census.gov/newsroom/stories/older-americans-month.html, via web search): 57.8M residents aged 65 and over in the 2022-07-01 estimates. 95.8e-5 x 57.8e6 = 55,372.4. Book checked first: lookup.py pool for Amyloid, ATTR, Transthyretin, Cardiomyopath, Polyneuropath and Amyloid Neuropathies returns nothing. No assumptions row exists on indications 64, 77, 80, 400, 401 or 402. The seeds of Wainua (eplontersen) and Vyndaqel carry no pool, and Amvuttra, Onpattro, Vyndamax, acoramidis, nucresiran and NTLA-2001 have no assumption rows. epidemiology.csv has no ATTR line. Wainua's 'roughly 12,000 diagnosed' sits in a revenue_ceiling note, is unsourced, and is not a pool. This is therefore the book's first ATTR-CM pool, confirmed against the paper itself rather than the nucresiran file. Caveats: the algorithm is an amyloidosis code plus HF, AF or cardiomyopathy. It is unvalidated and finds 'likely ATTR-CM', which the authors say may overestimate. 62% of the 2021 at-risk cohort was East North Central. Plausibility: Laires 2025 puts ATTR-CM at 41.1 (narrow) to 224.0 (broad) per million, 14,047 to 76,560 in the US. Tafamidis alone had 15,946 Part D beneficiaries in 2024 (Vyndamax 13,925 plus Vyndaqel 2,021, lookup.py demand), so the narrow figure is too low and 55,372 is plausible.

incidence.source: Alexander KM et al., J Am Heart Assoc 2026, PMID 42333670: incidence 44.3 per 100,000 person-years (95% CI 39.4-49.2) aged 65 and over in 2021, x 57.8mm = 25,605. Identical to the ALNY nucresiran seed
incidence.note: Kept identical to nucresiran for the same reason as prevalence
incidence.check: Alexander full text: incidence per 100,000 person-years '44.3 (95% CI, 39.6-49.5) in 2021 for the Medicare Database' (the abstract prints 39.4-49.2). Table 1: 314 cases among 734,819 at risk in 2021. 44.3e-5 x 57.8e6 = 25,605.4. The incidence rate ratio of 1.15 a year is confirmed. It matches the unverified nucresiran seed, which I checked against the paper, not the file.

eligible_pct.source: HLA filter: Intellia's genomic analysis of more than 600 trial samples found 'the highest observed liver transaminase elevations were in patients carrying one specific human leukocyte antigen (HLA) allele' (Intellia 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-337952, filed 2026-08-06), MD&A); the allele is HLA-C*05:01, carried by about 12% of the samples analysed, and each of the five highest elevations was in a carrier (Q2 2026 call, via BioSpace 'Intellia finds genetic suspect for liver safety signals with ATTR gene therapy' and Yahoo Finance's Q2 2026 call summary; read from search summaries). 1 - 0.12 = 0.88. Otherwise the label is expected to read as Amvuttra's: 'the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) in adults' (book labels table, setid 8db0facb-81b6-4006-9239-27dc6409c5d3)
eligible_pct.note: JUDGEMENT that carriers fall outside the label or decline, the abacavir precedent (the Ziagen label contraindicates use in HLA-B*5701 carriers). The filings say only that genotyping results will go to investigators and patients while Intellia engages the FDA. Case for higher: the FDA may require monitoring only, giving 1.0; most carriers had no severe elevation. Case for lower: the amended MAGNITUDE protocol also excludes 'certain liver abnormalities', recent cardiovascular instability and ejection fraction below 25% (8-K 0001193125-26-084309, EX-99.2, via search summary), none of them quantified here; the 12% is a trial-sample share, not a US population frequency
eligible_pct.check: Q2 2026 10-Q verbatim: a genomic analysis of 'more than 600 patient samples' found that 'the highest observed liver transaminase elevations were in patients carrying one specific human leukocyte antigen ("HLA") allele', and 'As we engage with the FDA ... we will provide HLA genotyping results to investigators and patients'. The allele and share come from a web search (Yahoo Finance Q2 2026 call summary; BioSpace): C*05:01. The summary reads 'Approximately 12% of the population carries the C*05:01 allele' (population, where the note says trial samples), 'the strong majority of C*05:01 positive patients did not experience severe transaminase elevations', and each of the five highest elevations was in a carrier. Management describes 'HLA typing to identify higher-risk patients and applying straightforward mitigation measures'. A second search found no FDA decision and no protocol exclusion of carriers. 1 - 0.12 = 0.88. Amvuttra's CM label wording is confirmed in the book's labels table (setid 8db0facb-81b6-4006-9239-27dc6409c5d3): 'the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) in adults'. A labelled judgement; management's mitigation language strengthens the stated case for 1.0. The MAGNITUDE amended exclusions (8-K 0001193125-26-084309 EX-99.2) are not in the book's filing_sections and were not re-checked. They appear only in the case-against note.

untreated_carryover_pct.unit: share of untreated eligible patients still eligible the next year
untreated_carryover_pct.source: stationary pool, the remternetug method: 55,372 / (55,372 + 25,605) = 0.6838. Same value as the ALNY nucresiran seed on this pool
untreated_carryover_pct.note: JUDGEMENT. ATTR-CM kills: 12% of vutrisiran starters died within 12 months in Optum (PMID 42455256). untreated_carryover_pct.check: 55,372 / (55,372 + 25,605) = 0.68380. Bart 2026 abstract: 13 of 111 (12%) died within 12 months. The stationary method is remternetug's. Alexander reports a prevalence odds ratio of 1.17 a year, which is the stated case for higher.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Incumbent: Amvuttra's US ATTR-CM launch (label 2025-03-20). US Amvuttra net sales were $361.346mm in Q2 2025 and $809.079mm in Q2 2026 (Alnylam 10-Q 0001178670-26-000062, book filing_sections). The pre-CM PN run rate is FY2024 US $630.613mm / 4 = $157.653mm a quarter (book asset_revenue_regions, 10-K 0001628280-26-007497). Net price per patient-year, from the book's demand rows (lookup.py demand Amvuttra, Part B 2024): $229,033,878.80 over 47,837.5 billing units of 1 mg is $4,787.75 a mg, $119,694 a 25 mg dose and $478,775 for four quarterly doses; less the 6% add-on, $451,674. Annualised CM run rates imply 1,804 and 5,769 patient-years on therapy. Exits are 20.72% a year: 13 deaths and 10 switches among 111 vutrisiran starters within 12 months (Bart NK et al., Adv Ther 2026, PMID 42455256). Starts over the year = 5,769 - 1,804 + 0.2072 x (1,804 + 5,769) / 2 = 4,750, or 5.87% a year of the pool of 55,372 + 25,605 = 80,977. Half of that is 0.0293
penetration_peak_pct.note: CORRECTED from 0.037. The researcher divided revenue by Part B spend per beneficiary ($379,824 / 1.06 = $358,324). The same demand row shows that a 2024 beneficiary received 47,837.5 / 25 / 603 = 3.17 of the 4 annual doses, so spend per beneficiary is 79% of a patient-year's cost, and the patient counts and start rates came out 1.26x too high (7.39% before, 5.87% now). Part D agrees: $118,225 a fill at 2.91 fills per beneficiary is $472,901 a year at four fills. JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 0.5 on Amvuttra. Against nex-z: one death and a genotype-linked liver signal in an elderly population, a permanent edit where a chronic drug can be stopped, HLA typing and liver monitoring, and a crowded field by 2031 (tafamidis possibly generic, acoramidis, vutrisiran, eplontersen, nucresiran, fibril depleters). For it: one infusion replaces lifelong dosing, and TTR fell 87% at 36 months in nine Phase 1 CM patients (10-Q). Case for higher: Alnylam's US net includes Medicaid and 340B discounts below ASP, so the true net per patient-year may be under $451,674, which would mean more patients. Q1 to Q2 2026 alone (Q1 US $702.554mm) annualises to 6.02%. Case for lower: the window includes pent-up second-line switching, which Alnylam says normalised in early 2026 (8-K 0001178670-26-000060, which lowered its 2026 TTR guidance). Komodo's lower exit rate of 15.5% (22 deaths, plus 142 stops less 53 restarts, of 718; PMID 42455256) gives 5.62%. The book's Casgevy seed peaks at 0.011. Engine check (eligible 0.88, ex-US 1.3365, carryover 0.6838, k 1.08, midpoint 3.2): about 1,980 US and 2,645 total CM starts a year from 2038, $3.7bn a year worldwide at $1.408mm
penetration_peak_pct.check: Revenue inputs confirmed in the book: Alnylam 10-Q 0001178670-26-000062 note 3 lists AMVUTTRA United States at $809,079 (Q2 2026) and $361,346 (Q2 2025) thousand, and $1,511,633 and $559,310 for the six months, so Q1 2026 was $702.554mm and Q1 2025 $197.964mm. asset_revenue_regions gives Amvuttra US FY2024 $630.613mm. Recomputed from lookup.py demand Amvuttra, as instructed: Part B 2024 is $229,033,878.80 in spending, 47,837.5 units and 603 beneficiaries. That is $4,787.75 a mg; 25 mg is one dose (Part D 2024 shows 596 units over 1,192 claims, 0.5 mL, one syringe per claim, and $118,225 a claim, which matches $119,694 a dose). Per beneficiary this is 3.17 doses; a patient-year is 4, costing $478,775 and $451,674 net of the add-on. The researcher's method reproduces exactly (2,274 and 7,272 on therapy, 5,987 starts, 7.39%). At the patient-year price it gives 1,804 and 5,769, 4,750 starts and 5.87%, so 0.5 x 5.865% = 0.0293. Using Q1 2025 ($197.964mm) as the PN base instead gives 5.77%. Exits: Bart 2026 abstract, 23 of 111 left vutrisiran within 12 months (20.72%). Engine rerun with forecast.derive_new_patients: CM worldwide starts 85, 237, 598, 1,238, 1,938, 2,386, 2,574, 2,633 and 2,645 over 2030 to 2038.

ramp_steepness.check: lookup.py seed MK-1045: k 1.08 and midpoint 2.2 from 'Enhertu's own launch, fitted'. lookup.py demand Enhertu Part B beneficiaries: 864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105, 8,410 (2020-2024), confirmed. Same curve as the verified lonvo-z seed. A labelled reuse.

ramp_midpoint_year.source: Enhertu fit's 2.2 years (as ramp_steepness) plus 1.0 year because ATTR-CM launches a year after ATTRv-PN (forecast_start_year note)
ramp_midpoint_year.note: JUDGEMENT on the offset. The logistic leaks 3.1% of peak into 2030, before a CM approval (about 110 patients in the engine), a small overstatement
ramp_midpoint_year.check: 2.2 + 1.0 = 3.2. s_curve(0) / peak = 1 / (1 + exp(1.08 x 3.2)) = 0.0306, matching the stated 3.1%. At the corrected peak (0.0293) the engine puts about 85 CM patients worldwide into 2030, not about 110.

prevalence.source: Laires PA et al., 'Prevalence and incidence of amyloid transthyretin amyloidosis in the USA: insights from claims databases and electronic health records', Open Heart 2025, doi:10.1136/openhrt-2025-003781, PMID 41469145 (full text, PMC12766817): 2022 ATTR-PN prevalence 15.1 per million on the narrow definition (Clarivate Real-World Data, adults, census-adjusted). x 341,784,857 US residents on 2025-07-01 (Census Bureau Vintage 2025, the base the book's other seeds use) = 5,161
prevalence.note: This block is hATTRv-PN (MAGNITUDE-2, NCT06672237). Not carried by the book (lookup.py pool Amyloid, Polyneuropath return nothing; epidemiology.csv has no row). The ATTR-PN cohort includes the mixed phenotype (PN-only 6.0 plus mixed 9.8 per million), which overlaps the CM block by about 3,349 patients; PN-only alone (2,051) would sit below the roughly 2,300 US patients the 2024 PN market already treated (Amvuttra US $630.6mm at $358,324 is 1,760 patient-years, plus Onpattro $74.8mm and Wainua $85mm), so the wider cohort is used. Laires does not split variant from wild-type; the narrow definition is the conservative one (broad reads 47.3 per million). The eplontersen seed's 'roughly 12,000 diagnosed' US patients is unsourced and not used
prevalence.check: Laires 2025 full text (PMC12766817, doi:10.1136/openhrt-2025-003781): 2022 prevalence per million on the narrow definitions is ATTR-PN 15.1, ATTR-PN only 6.0 and ATTR-mixed 9.8 (broad 47.3). Patients are 18 and over and the rates are census-adjusted. 15.1 x 341.784857 = 5,160.9. The Census Vintage 2025 figure of 341,784,857 is the one the verified adimanebart seed confirmed on census.gov. The phenotype cohorts are defined separately and are not additive (6.0 + 9.8 = 15.8, not 15.1), so 'PN-only 6.0 plus mixed 9.8' is loose. The CM overlap, 9.8 x 341.78 = 3,349, is right. The book carries no PN pool (see the Amyloidosis prevalence check). Treated-patient test at the corrected patient-year price: Amvuttra's FY2024 US $630.613mm is 1,396 patient-years. Adding Onpattro ($74.787mm at its $286,149 Part B spend per beneficiary, about 261) and Wainua ($85mm at $226,539, about 375) gives about 2,030. That still roughly equals the PN-only count of 2,051, so the argument for the wider cohort holds.

incidence.source: Laires PA et al., Open Heart 2025, PMID 41469145: 2022 ATTR-PN incidence 3.5 per million, narrow definition, x 341,784,857 = 1,196

incidence.check: Laires full text: 2022 ATTR-PN incidence 3.5 per million on the narrow definition. Over 2019-2022 ATTR-PN incidence changed by +3.0% narrow ('No major changes were reported for the other phenotypes'). 3.5 x 341.784857 = 1,196.2.

eligible_pct.source: as the Amyloidosis block: HLA-C*05:01 carriers about 12% of more than 600 trial samples (Intellia 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-337952, filed 2026-08-06), MD&A; call details via search summaries). Label otherwise expected to read as Amvuttra's PN indication, 'the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults' (book labels table, setid 8db0facb-81b6-4006-9239-27dc6409c5d3), with no stage restriction
eligible_pct.note: JUDGEMENT, as the CM block. Case for lower: the label is hereditary only and Laires does not split variant from wild-type; mixed-phenotype patients coded with neuropathy may be wild-type or V142I carriers whose neuropathy has another cause (41% of 82 V142I carriers at Penn had PN, 13% possibly or probably from amyloid; PMID 42048769)
eligible_pct.check: The HLA inputs are as in the Amyloidosis block (10-Q verbatim; C*05:01 and about 12% from web search summaries; no FDA decision found). The PN label wording is confirmed in the book's labels table (Amvuttra 1.1, 'the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (hATTR-PN) in adults'). Dvorak 2026 (PMID 42048769 abstract): of 82 V142I carriers, 41% had PN and 13% had PN possibly or probably from amyloidosis, confirmed. Laires does not split variant from wild-type (full text: 'analysis of data relative to wild-type versus mutated TTR was not performed'), the stated case for lower. A labelled judgement.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Incumbent: Amvuttra's US hATTR-PN launch (June 2022), before its CM label. US net sales were $411.169mm in FY2023 and $630.613mm in FY2024 (book asset_revenue_regions, 10-K 0001628280-26-007497). At $451,674 net per patient-year (lookup.py demand Amvuttra, Part B 2024: $4,787.75 a mg x 100 mg a year / 1.06, as the Amyloidosis block), that is 910 and 1,396 patient-years on therapy. Starts in 2024 = 1,396 - 910 + 0.2072 x (910 + 1,396) / 2 = 725, exits from Bart 2026 (PMID 42455256). Over the pool of 5,161 + 1,196 = 6,357, that is 11.40% a year. Half of that is 0.0570
penetration_peak_pct.note: CORRECTED from 0.0719. The same fix as the CM block: spend per beneficiary covers 3.17 of 4 annual doses, so the researcher's 1,147 and 1,760 on therapy and 14.37% start rate were 1.26x too high. The claims agree on trend: CMS beneficiaries (Part B plus D) rose from 673 to 1,012 in 2024 (+50%), in line with the 53% rise in US revenue. JUDGEMENT: the same 0.5 multiple as the CM block, for the same reasons. The 2024 starts include switches from Onpattro (US sales fell from $97.7mm to $74.8mm) and off-label cardiac use (70% of Optum vutrisiran starters had heart failure; PMID 42455256), both cases for lower. Komodo's 15.5% exit rate gives 10.45%. Engine check (eligible 0.88, ex-US 1.3365, carryover 0.8119, k 1.08, midpoint 2.2): starts peak near 374 a year worldwide (about 280 US) in 2036
penetration_peak_pct.check: asset_revenue_regions confirms Amvuttra US FY2023 $411.169mm and FY2024 $630.613mm, and Onpattro US $97.739mm and $74.787mm. lookup.py demand Amvuttra gives Part B 478 beneficiaries in 2023 and 603 in 2024, and Part D 195 and 409. Researcher's method reproduced: 1,147 and 1,760 on therapy, 914 starts, 14.37%. At the patient-year price ($451,674, derived from the same Part B row): 910.3 and 1,396.2 patient-years, 724.8 starts, 11.40%, so 0.5 x 11.40% = 0.0570. Engine rerun: PN worldwide starts 36, 91, 188, 291, 352, 372 and 374 over 2030 to 2036. With the CM block, total product revenue peaks at about $4.24bn in 2038 (US $3.17bn), against the researcher's $5.27bn, before the 0.695 share and PoS.
